what: Each panel gets only a long scroll stretch while the visible stage stays pinned to the screen and overlaps the others. When a panel’s top touches the top of the screen, the stage that was on scales up to 1.05 and turns off over .5s, then the new stage turns on from 1.05 → 1 over .5s (power1.out). If the body text is taller than the window inside the stage, the stretch grows by that much. While scrolling through the middle of the stretch, the text flows upward inside the window with the top and bottom 10% faded by a mask (scrub). Scrolling back above the first panel or past the last panel turns the stage off.

options.dur: Length of each off and on phase (sec), default .5
options.scale: Scale-up factor when fading out, default 1.05
options.--fx-panel-h: Scroll length of one section (css), default 200svh — never shorter than the screen height
options.--fx-window-gap: Window height = Screen height minus this value (css), default 40svh

note: When the stage turns on it fires fx:enter (bubbling) from the section element, and fx:leave when it turns off — used to move the menu underline to the section id. The stage is position: fixed, so use it on window-scroll pages.
